heroHeadline: Drivers' confederation calls national 24-hour strike for Sep 28 over diesel price hike; Santa Cruz agricultural sectors issue blockade ultimatum as boliviano climbs to Bs. 12.06/$1
heroSubtitle: Highways stayed clear of blockades through Sept. 22 despite continued police and military deployment on the La Paz-Oruro, Oruro-Cochabamba and El Alto-Tiquina corridors, but pressure over Decree 5716's diesel-subsidy elimination kept building on multiple fronts: El Alto's driver federation proposed an indefinite strike at its Sept. 22 assembly, sugarcane and rice growers plus valley producers around Montero (Santa Cruz) gave the government a blockade ultimatum the same day, and on Sept. 23 the Confederación Sindical de Choferes de Bolivia, led by Lucio Gómez, formally called a 24-hour national transport stoppage for Monday, Sept. 28 — warning "el lunes no habrá transporte público en el país" and threatening escalation to an indefinite general strike if the government does not respond. The government countered that 80.3% of public-transport vehicles don't depend exclusively on diesel and dispatched regional ministers to explain the measure. The boliviano continued weakening, rising from Bs. 11.00/$1 on Sept. 20 to Bs. 11.90 on Sept. 22 and Bs. 12.06 on Sept. 23 on the central bank's official rate.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
